Run a complete multi-omics factor analysis workflow in one call

Source: R/factomics.R
factomics.Rd

Fits the requested factor methods with run_factor_pipeline(), then (when asked) attaches metadata, embeds the factor scores (PCA / UMAP / t-SNE), clusters the samples on each method's factors, and benchmarks the methods against each other.

Usage

factomics(
  X,
  metadata = NULL,
  sample_col = "sample",
  methods = c("PCA", "MFA", "FABIA", "GFA"),
  k = 5,
  embeddings = c("umap", "tsne"),
  cluster_method = "kmeans",
  n_clusters = 2:6,
  benchmark = TRUE,
  seed = 21,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

X

Named list of features x samples matrices (or one matrix).

metadata

Optional data frame of sample annotations.

sample_col

Sample-ID column of metadata (default "sample").

methods

Factor methods to run; see list_factor_methods().

k

Number of factors (default 5).

embeddings

Any of "umap", "tsne", "pca"; NULL to skip.

cluster_method

"kmeans", "hclust" or "pam"; NULL to skip.

n_clusters

Candidate numbers of clusters (default 2:6).

benchmark

Logical. Run benchmark_factor_methods() when at least two methods were fitted (default TRUE).

seed

Random seed (default 21).

verbose

Logical. Print progress (default TRUE).

...

Further arguments for run_factor_pipeline() (e.g. fabia_alpha, gfa_iter_max, mofa_python).

Value

An object of class factomics (a list) with elements results, metadata, embeddings, clusters, cluster_agreement and benchmark.

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiomics(n_samples = 45, seed = 1)
fx  <- factomics(sim$data, metadata = sim$metadata,
                 methods = c("PCA", "MFA"), k = 3,
                 embeddings = "pca", benchmark = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
fx
#> <factomics workflow>
#> <factomics_results>
#>   45 samples, 3 view(s): transcriptome (200), metabolome (80), microbiome (50)
#>   PCA       3 factors
#>   MFA       3 factors
#>   Embeddings: PCA 
#>   Clustering:
#>             method algorithm k silhouette
#>                PCA    kmeans 4      0.468
#>                MFA    kmeans 4      0.466
#>  Concatenated data    kmeans 3      0.133
